title: Present Simple · Everyday English
subtitle: Present Simple, adverbs of frequency, translation and the verb to be

blocks.title: Make the sentence negative and write a question
blocks.text: Follow the example. Example: She works here. → She doesn’t work here. / Does she work here?

blocks.title: Present Simple: negative + question
blocks.instructions: Write two answers for every sentence.

items.prompt: I often meet this patient here.
answers: I don't often meet this patient here.
Do I often meet this patient here?
items.explanation: I don't often meet this patient here. / Do I often meet this patient here?

items.prompt: She usually checks vital signs in the morning.
answers: She doesn't usually check vital signs in the morning.
Does she usually check vital signs in the morning?
items.explanation: She doesn't usually check vital signs in the morning. / Does she usually check vital signs in the morning?

items.prompt: They often read medical textbooks at home.
answers: They don't often read medical textbooks at home.
Do they often read medical textbooks at home?
items.explanation: They don't often read medical textbooks at home. / Do they often read medical textbooks at home?

items.prompt: He always gives patients their prescriptions.
answers: He doesn't always give patients their prescriptions.
Does he always give patients their prescriptions?
items.explanation: He doesn't always give patients their prescriptions. / Does he always give patients their prescriptions?

blocks.title: Adverbs of frequency
blocks.text: Choose all options that make the sentence natural. Example: I don’t often work nights. → sometimes / usually can change the meaning but remain grammatical.

blocks.title: Replace “often”
blocks.instructions: Choose all options that work naturally in the sentence.

items.prompt: We don't often have dictations at our nursing class.
They don't often speak Russian at work.
I don't often read English medical journals.

blocks.title: Translate into English
blocks.text: Write the full sentence. Example: Я обычно работаю утром. → I usually work in the morning.

items.prompt: Что ты обычно читаешь по утрам?
items.answer: What do you usually read in the morning?
items.explanation: What do you usually read in the morning?

items.prompt: Она часто встречает коллег после работы.
items.answer: She often meets her colleagues after work.
items.explanation: She often meets her colleagues after work.
acceptedAnswers: She often meets colleagues after work.
She often meets her colleagues after work.

items.prompt: Читают ли твои пациенты инструкции к лекарствам?
items.answer: Do your patients read the instructions for their medication?
items.explanation: Do your patients read the instructions for their medication?
acceptedAnswers: Do your patients read the instructions for their medication?
Do your patients read medication instructions?

items.prompt: Мы обычно не говорим по-русски в больнице.
items.answer: We usually don't speak Russian at the hospital.
items.explanation: We usually don't speak Russian at the hospital.
acceptedAnswers: We usually don't speak Russian at the hospital.
We don't usually speak Russian at the hospital.

items.prompt: Что ты делаешь каждое утро перед работой?
items.answer: What do you do every morning before work?
items.explanation: What do you do every morning before work?

blocks.title: The verb “to be”
blocks.text: Choose the correct form. Example: I ___ a nurse. → am

items.prompt: She ___ a nurse at City Hospital.
___ you from Russia?
The patients ___ in room 204.
I ___ not a doctor. I ___ a registered nurse.
___ the doctor in the clinic right now?

blocks.title: Short answers about you
blocks.text: These answers are saved for the teacher but are not graded automatically.

items.prompt: What do you usually read in the morning — news, social media, or medical materials?
items.placeholder: Example: I usually read the news on my phone.

items.prompt: Do you often speak English at home?
items.placeholder: Example: I sometimes speak English at home.

items.prompt: Where do you usually study English — at home, on the bus, or during breaks?
items.placeholder: Example: I usually study English at home.

items.prompt: Do you always understand American nurses when they speak fast?
items.placeholder: Example: No, I don’t always understand them.

items.prompt: What do you usually do after your English class?
items.placeholder: Example: I review new words after class.
